projects.name: GateOrchestra
projects.overview: A lightweight, trainable gate that sits in front of a multi-agent orchestrator and decides, before any expensive compute is spent, whether a cheap single-agent answer is good enough.
projects.problem: Multi-agent systems such as ReAct, Debate and Reflexion can improve answers, but running them on every task burns far more tokens than a single agent — often for no gain.
projects.solution: A CoT self-consistency probe answers first. A gate trained on pre-execution signals then chooses STOP (keep the probe answer) or ESCALATE to the full multi-agent orchestrator, with the escalation budget capped at k × the probe's tokens.
architecture: Probe agent — CoT self-consistency, 3 samples
Feature extractor — 8 pre-execution features
Gate — learned (LogReg / GBT / MLP), rule-based or random
MAS orchestrator — ReAct, Debate, Reflexion sub-agents
Token accountant — budgets enforced before every call
FastAPI backend and React + three.js console
features: STOP / ESCALATE gating calibrated over accuracy tolerance and budget multiplier
ReAct, Debate and Reflexion sub-agents behind one orchestrator
Optional LinUCB contextual-bandit strategy router
True provider token totals with pre-call budget enforcement
Wilson confidence intervals and exact McNemar tests
Honest results reporting — no verified real-LLM headline yet; simulated figures are labelled as such
contribution: Owned the agent layer (Person 2): CoT-SC probe agent, MAS orchestrator and the ReAct, Debate and Reflexion sub-agents
Added the LinUCB contextual bandit router, early exit and semantic soft voting
Integrated the Groq cloud provider with an Ollama local fallback
Retrained the GBT gate on real Groq traces
Built the batch evaluation pipeline and the agent performance / error analysis modules

projects.name: WhoToTrust
projects.tagline: When labels disagree, who should you trust?
projects.overview: LabelTriage decides, vote by vote, whether a disagreement between human annotators is a mistake or a genuine difference of opinion — then trains on each differently.
projects.problem: Pipelines either delete minority votes as noise or keep every vote as a soft label. Both are wrong part of the time: some disagreement is error, some is real ambiguity.
projects.solution: Score each vote's probability of being an error from five evidence groups, then route each item to a hard label (clear), a soft label (ambiguous) or a down-weighted target (unreliable).
architecture: AmbiNoise benchmark — real many-annotator votes with injected, labelled errors
Five evidence groups — vote split, annotator reliability, model plausibility, neighbours, probe learning
Calibrated out-of-fold error model and three-way router
Harm analysis via counterfactual retraining
Python API and React explorer
features: Benchmark over CIFAR-10H images and ChaosNLI text, with VariErr NLI as a transfer test
Spammer, swap, lazy and plausible-wrong error processes
On images, beats majority vote and soft labels for every error type, within about 1 point of the oracle
Web explorer for every item, vote, error score and the reasons behind it
Runs end to end on a laptop CPU; 219 Python tests plus unit and end-to-end web tests
contribution: Sole author — method, benchmark, experiments, web app and tests

projects.name: NeuroLens
projects.subtitle: TopoCircuit-SAE
projects.tagline: Looking inside language models: multi-parent feature absorption in sparse autoencoders
projects.overview: A mechanistic-interpretability study that measures how sparse autoencoders hide general concepts inside specific ones when a token has several parents, and tests whether DAG routing reduces it.
projects.problem: Feature absorption — a specific latent silently taking over a general one — has only been measured with single-parent tasks, yet real concepts have several parents at once.
projects.solution: MPAbs, a benchmark with three parents per token on real Pythia-70M activations, and DR-SAE, an autoencoder that learns an acyclic parent graph between latents and routes each child's activation to its ancestors.
architecture: Activation extraction from Pythia-70M, layer 3
Seven SAE variants trained on identical data
MPAbs benchmark scored per parent and jointly
Synthetic tier with known ground-truth graph
Circuit faithfulness test on subject–verb agreement
Local API, SQLite and interactive explorer
features: Pre-registered hypotheses, with falsified results reported openly
DR-SAE leaves a parent latent silent 37% less often than Matryoshka at matched effective L0 (exploratory)
Interactive DAG hierarchy explorer and routing simulator
Runs entirely on CPU; paper source generated from results
contribution: Sole author — research design, models, benchmark, experiments, explorer and paper

projects.name: Cost-Aware Agent Router
projects.tagline: Route every query to the cheapest agent that can handle it
projects.overview: A confidence-based, four-tier LLM routing cascade that starts each query at the lowest-cost capable tier and escalates only when confidence is too low and budget allows.
projects.problem: Sending every query to a frontier model wastes money; sending everything to a small model fails on reasoning, code and strict structured output.
projects.solution: Classify complexity to pick a starting tier, score the answer's confidence from syntax checks and hedging detection, and escalate through Cheap → RAG → Frontier → Consensus only when needed.
architecture: Complexity pre-classifier
Four agent tiers — Cheap, RAG, Frontier, Consensus
Confidence evaluator — syntactic + semantic hedging
Cost tracker and per-step latency profiling
FastAPI service with SQLite audit logs and a live dashboard
features: Dynamic escalation with step-by-step audit trail
Token-level cost and latency tracking
Daily and monthly budget controls with policy sliders
Offline deterministic mock mode plus live providers
Benchmark harness with Wilson confidence intervals (mock mode validates routing and cost, not real accuracy)
contribution: Sole author — router, agents, evaluation, API and dashboard

projects.name: Compute Bazaar
projects.tagline: A combinatorial auction market where AI agents bid for compute
projects.overview: An AI-agent compute marketplace where agents place budget-aware bundle bids for GPU, CPU, RAM and API budget, and allocation is solved as a combinatorial auction with VCG pricing.
projects.problem: Queue-based schedulers block high-value jobs behind early arrivals, and per-unit spot markets leave agents holding half a bundle they cannot use.
projects.solution: Treat allocation as a winner-determination problem solved by binary integer linear programming, with VCG Clarke-pivot pricing so truthful bidding pays off, plus fairness tracking against starvation.
architecture: Agent layer — Coding, Research, Data and Analysis agents with optional Groq reasoning
Auction engine — PuLP / CBC ILP solver and VCG pricing
Marketplace with scarcity pricing and fairness tracker
FastAPI gateway with JWT / API-key auth and WebSocket feed
SQLAlchemy persistence and Chart.js dashboard
features: Atomic bundle bids — no partial allocations
VCG pricing with adaptive bidding strategies
Jain fairness index and anti-starvation guards
In a seeded 25-round simulation, highest social welfare and utilisation of five schedulers (38% above round-robin)
Live WebSocket dashboard with bidding ticker and round history
contribution: Sole author — auction engine, agents, API, dashboard and benchmarks

projects.name: JOCKY Forensics
projects.tagline: A domain-specific language for safe, verifiable forensic triage
projects.award: Winner — Smart India Hackathon 2026 Internal Hackathon
projects.overview: A domain-specific language and execution framework for authorized, read-only computer and network forensic analysis across Windows, Linux and macOS, built for SIH problem statement SIH26148.
projects.problem: Ad-hoc admin scripts used during incident response are fragile, hard to reproduce and frequently trip antivirus and EDR alerts.
projects.solution: Investigators write declarative JOCKY scripts that compile to a validated intermediate representation and run only read-only collectors; evidence is sealed with SHA-256 and tracked through a chain of custody.
architecture: JOCKY DSL — lexer, recursive-descent parser, validator, IR v1.0
IR executor with read-only policy and hardening
Cross-platform collectors and authenticated endpoint agent
Evidence vault with SHA-256 verification and custody log
Correlation, timeline and MITRE ATT&CK mapping
Report engine and React dashboard
features: Windows, Linux and macOS evidence collection
SHA-256 integrity sealing and tamper detection
Chain-of-custody tracking
Endpoint agent with pairing, heartbeat and job polling
JSON, HTML and Markdown forensic reports
contribution: Sole author of the repository — language, engine, collectors, vault, analysis and dashboard
